- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (0.00–0.20), model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast slope or adding downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85.00), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply lagged mean reversion or cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., 0.20–0.40), model frequently overreacts; reduce forecast magnitude or introduce smoothing to avoid overcorrection.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early days (e.g., first 5–7 days); apply downward adjustment for first 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model often fails to capture volatility; introduce stochastic or volatility-adjusted correction factor.
